Hello Mike,

Thanks for spotting this conversion error! I took Mg for mg when converting from kg/m3... So, mussel density is 1.086 g/cm3. Not lower than air obviously :)
However, it seems like it doesn't solve the problem (see updated figure attached, it's a bit better though!).

I thought of setting two types of layers (one for mussels and one for the rock underneath) but I wanted to make it simple since I don't have the information about the type of rocks for all of my sites yet.
But I guess we can assume it's a type of granite for now and update the code with site-specific information later (see updated script below).
Could you confirm I set the two types of layer properly?

Regarding the roughness height parameter, I thought we could use an approximation (e.g., 0.1xheight based on Hansen, F.V., 1993. Surface Roughness Lengths. Report ARL-TR-61. Army Research Laboratory), but I imagine it's a bit more complicated. Let me know if you have a better value to suggest for rocky shores.

Here is the updated code:

Jonathan

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jonathan,

The other thing that might be worth investigating is whether you've got the zenith angles set up properly. You're using hourly inputs and you've set the zenith angle input to -1 which triggers the microclimate model to calculate the zenith angles, but that only works if your input data starts at midnight. Otherwise you need to pre-compute the zenith angles (you can do this with the microclima package).

Anyhow, to make it easier, can you put an example together for a simulation that fails, where you save the 'microin' list as an Rda file (an R data file), and attach it, so it's just a matter of loading that file and running the model? Then it will be easier to see what might be going wrong.

All the best,
Mike

I now pre-compute hourly zenith angles as follows (very similar to microclima):
ZENhr <- zenith(s=solar(as.POSIXct(data$datetime)), lon=longlat[1], lat=longlat[2]) # from GeoLight package

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jonathon,

The ERR parameter is controlling when the numerical integrator is satisfied with its solution of the heat budget - by increasing it you're getting a less accurate calculation so ideally you keep it as low as possible. Five isn't too out there, but I have rarely needed to alter it from the default of 1.5 except in the case of simulating snow, suggesting something's awry. I just scanned your parameters again, though, and you have 2800 g/cm2 for the density of the rock - that could well be the problem (should be 2.8). The other thing that would be worth doing is a check against e.g. the output of micro_ncep for a particular site, with default settings and then gradually trying to make it come closer to your specific settings, to make sure it's all looking ok. Check carefully how the plots of soil temp. vs. time look as you go to make sure nothing weird is going on. Always good to start from somewhere that you have confidence is working properly, and then modify gradually. It's so easy for issues to creep in with this kind of modelling.

Hello everyone,

I'm a master's student interested in using DEB theory with NicheMapR. I cannot understand how to calculate the thermal response parameters: Arrhenius lower boundary (T_L),  Arrhenius upper boundary (T_H) and their respective Arrhenius temperatures (TAL, TAH).

I would like to determine the parameters for the anchovy Engraulis japonicus. However, when I run the "run_my_species.m" file I do not get any temperature parameters output in the "results.mat" file. I have also searched for a DEBtool routine but could not find one.

I have read the DEBvignette, DEBtool manual and AmP Estimation pages. I see these parameters mentioned but no explanation of how they're calculated. I feel like I'm missing something obvious - any help or advice would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,

Neil Waters

Hi Neil,

If you have data on rates as a function of temperature, and they are across a great enough range of temperatures that you can see how the rate drops past the optimum at the high end, and if anything unusual is happening at the cold end, then you can fit the parameters. It can be done via the DEB estimation process (but you have to modify the pars_init file to include these parameters - that current entry for the anchovy you're working on only has the Arrhenius temperature, not the other four). But you can also do it using the instructions at this link:

http://www.debtheory.org/wiki/index.php?title=Get_environmental_temperatures

and in the attached document.

All the best,
Mike
